query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by the formation of a stable, dense oxide layer on the surface, which acts as a barrier to corrosion and wear, and this layer is influenced by the alloy's composition, particularly the addition of elements such as Mo, Si, and Zr.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys with varying compositions, including AlCoCrFeNi, FeCoNiCuAl, and CoCrFeMoNi, in their as-cast or annealed state
generation.intervention: Addition of elements such as Mo, Si, and Zr to the alloy composition, and varying the content of these elements
generation.conditions: Harsh corrosive mechanical environments, including high-temperature and high-humidity conditions, and exposure to corrosive media such as 3.5% NaCl solution
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a stable, dense oxide layer on the surface of the alloy, composed of oxides such as ZrTiO4 and Cr2O3
generation.mechanism: The oxide layer acts as a barrier to corrosion and wear, reducing the diffusion of corrosive species and the adhesion of wear particles, and the alloy's composition influences the formation and stability of this layer
generation.predicted_outcome: A decrease in wear rate and corrosion current density, with a predicted reduction of 20-30% in wear rate and 10-20% in corrosion current density, compared to a baseline alloy without the added elements
generation.baseline: A high-entropy alloy without the addition of elements such as Mo, Si, and Zr, such as AlCoCrFeNi or FeCoNiCuAl
generation.boundary: The predicted outcome should hold for high-entropy alloys with varying compositions, including AlCoCrFeNi, FeCoNiCuAl, and CoCrFeMoNi, and for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, including high-temperature and high-humidity conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of the oxide layer formation and its influence on wear and corrosion resistance is not fully understood, and further research is needed to clarify the relationships between alloy composition, oxide layer formation, and wear and corrosion resistance

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled comparison of the wear and corrosion resistance of high-entropy alloys with and without the addition of elements such as Mo, Si, and Zr, using techniques such as sliding wear tests and electrochemical corrosion tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate and corrosion current density of the alloy with the added elements are not significantly lower than those of the baseline alloy, or if the oxide layer is not stable and dense, then the hypothesis is falsified, with a threshold of 10% reduction in wear rate and corrosion current density

cited_evidence.text: AbstractThe aim of the paper is to study the Zr addition effect on the mechanical properties and corrosion behavior of a high-entropy alloy from the CoCrFeMoNi system. This alloy was designed to be used for components in the geothermal industry that are exposed to high temperature and corrosion. Two alloys, one Zr-free (named Sample 1) and another one doped with 0.71 wt.% Zr (named Sample 2), were obtained in a vacuum arc remelting equipment from high-purity granular raw materials. Microstructural characterization and quantitative analysis by SEM and EDS were performed. The Young modulus values for the experimental alloys were calculated on the basis of a three-point bending test. Corrosion behavior was estimated by linear polarization test and by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The addition of Zr resulted in a decrease in the value of the Young modulus but also in a decrease in corrosion resistance. The beneficial effect of Zr on the microstructure was the grain refinement, and this ensured a good deoxidation of the alloy.Keywords: HEA, CoCrFeMoNiZr, microstructure, corrosion, EIS, Young modulus

AbstractIn the quest of new materials that can withstand severe irradiation and mechanical extremes for advanced applications (e.g. fission & fusion reactors, space applications, etc.), design, prediction and control of advanced materials beyond current material designs become paramount. Here, through a combined experimental and simulation methodology, we design a nanocrystalline refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) system. Compositions assessed under extreme environments and in situ electron-microscopy reveal both high thermal stability and radiation resistance. We observe grain refinement under heavy ion irradiation and resistance to dual-beam irradiation and helium implantation in the form of low defect generation and evolution, as well as no detectable grain growth. cited_evidence.text: This result indicates the high wear resistance of the HEA. The enhanced wear resistance in this study may be associated with the high microhardness of the BCC and Laves phases. Moreover, in situ reinforcing carbides of Nb (NbC) and Ti-Mo (Ti0.5Mo0.5C) are also expected to enhance the wear resistance of the alloy, as observed in some earlier reports [,]. Highly wear-resistant materials are required for orthopedic applications to minimize debris accumulation [] and metal allergy [] due to the accumulation of metallic ions from wear debris. The totality of the experimental results and discussions indicate that microstructural design through the selection of the constituent elements greatly influenced the microhardness, compressive and wear properties of the alloy. It can be concluded that the mechanical, bio-corrosion, and wear-resistance properties of the CrMoNbTiZr HEA developed in this study showed a good propensity for application as a biomaterial.

In this work, we have shown that an HEA film can be synthesized from a single partially spark-plasma-sintered target. Such use of single target sputtering was beneficial for synthesizing nanocrystalline films with low grain sizes and superior mechanical properties. The addition of Cu to the RHEA film was shown to increase the hardness and nanopillar compressional strength. The CuMoTaWV RHEA film showed an average hardness and nanopillar compressive strength of 19 ± 2.3 and 10 ± 0.8 GPa, respectively, which are ∼20% higher than those of the reported RHEA films in the literature. The high hardness and compressional strength of the reported film were attributed to nanocrystalline grain size and grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation. The wear behavior and adhesion of the CuMoTaWV film on a steel substrate were improved by annealing at 300 °C, and it showed improved coefficient of friction and wear resistance at RT and 300 °C. The reported results suggest that RHEA films can be beneficial for wear and nanopillar applications.

The simultaneous improvement of mechanical and corrosion resistance is of great significance for engineering applications. In this work, a novel lightweight amorphous structure AlTiVNb high-entropy alloy (HEA) film was fabricated by magnetron sputtering. The compression test of the AlTiVNb HEA film nanopillar exhibits a high compressive strength of up to 3.6 GPa and deformability approaching 58%. The high strength is affected by the disordered state, the nanostructure, and the lattice distortion effect, while the high ductility comes from the ductile shear band and the island structure. In addition, the AlTiVNb HEA film shows a current density of 4.90 × 10−8 A/cm2 and a potential of −0.234 V in the 3.5% NaCl solution, comparable to that of the 316L stainless steel. The chemical disorder state, cocktail effect, and homogeneous amorphous structure contribute to excellent corrosion resistance. This finding offers new insights into high-performance HEA films with robust mechanical and anticorrosion performances for microelectronic devices and mechanical metamaterials.
